framing: An indie-hacker chasing $10k MRR finds He Was Socrates impossible to monetize: every CLAUDE.md invariant (NO-CLOUD, abstention-as-product, Korean 평어체 lock, no photoreal) refuses paid-tier gating. The honest pricing page is the punchline — three tiers, all $0, all current plan, with a Donate sidebar replacing the upgrade CTA.
target_persona: Kaggle/DeepMind judges who have seen forty SaaS pricing tables this morning and would notice a pricing page whose price is the joke; secondary — Two-Weeks-Team members who recognize the indie-hacker SaaS template instantly and read the inversion as commentary on what 'free software' actually costs to monetize; tertiary — GitHub drive-bys who arrive expecting a paywall and leave understanding that abstention extends from the model to the business model.
primary_surface: Indie-hacker SaaS pricing chrome inverted: 3-tier pricing table (Personal / Team / School District), every column labeled $0/month, every column carrying an identical 'Current plan' badge, identical feature checklist across tiers (because no feature is gateable under the invariants), and a Donate-to-Two-Weeks-Team sidebar replacing the upgrade CTA. Stripe-shaped UI, GitHub Sponsors / Open Collective links as the only monetization. Korean confined to the bust subtitle in a corner; English everywhere else (pricing chrome convention).
opus_4_7_capability: Long-context narrative coherence — Opus 4.7 holds the contradiction across the page: maintain authentic indie-hacker SaaS pricing-table affordances (tier columns, feature comparison, FAQ, current-plan state) while every component telegraphs the inversion (every price $0, every tier 'current', every feature shared, every upgrade CTA replaced by a donate link). The footnote ("We considered a paid tier. We could not name a feature worth gating.") only lands if the surrounding chrome is dead-serious pricing UI.
mvp_scope: Single-file pricing page with: (1) three-tier comparison table with identical feature lists, (2) 'Current plan' badge on every tier (not just Personal), (3) feature matrix across 9 rows showing identical checks, (4) Donate sidebar with GitHub Sponsors + Open Collective placeholders pointing to Two-Weeks-Team, (5) footnote explaining the inversion, (6) Korean 평어체 bust subtitle in a corner, (7) hero metric strip citing the 4 monetizable concerns (결제·해지·환불·invoice) and showing each as N/A, (8) FAQ that answers 'How do you make money?' with 'We don't.'
one_liner_pitch: The indie-hacker pricing page where every tier is $0, every plan is current, and the upgrade CTA is replaced by GitHub Sponsors — because no invariant survives a paywall.
spec_alignment_notes: All idea.spec.json fields populated (_filled_ratio=1.0); followed spec verbatim with persona-bias overlay. target_persona narrows the spec's primary judges to those who recognize the SaaS pricing template (consistent with secondary 'general dev audience'). primary_surface honors the spec's single-file self-contained HTML constraint and chooses pricing-table form per persona dispatch_brief — the indie-hacker bias ($10k MRR target) is expressed through the inversion rather than through actual monetization (which would violate the project's free-software stance). Korean-surface policy honored: 평어체 limited to bust subtitle corner; pricing chrome remains English per spec.language_policy. Anti-patterns refused: no marketing superlatives in the pricing chrome ('Most Popular' / 'Best Value' replaced by deadpan 'Current plan'); no fake metrics; the four pillars (결제·해지·환불·invoice) shown as N/A with citations to the absent infrastructure rather than fabricated.
